stage: integration (diarrhea) check of the 13 absorb components
method: Read-only. Every absorb component was compared against the actual OAW V2 code, tests, templates, bundled EGM bridges and vendored EGM upstream, AGENTS.md, templates/AGENTS.md, the README principles, DECISIONS.md and docs/plans/skill-catalog-execution.md. No food code, installer, hook, build or test was run, and no OAW code was run. Measurements came from wc, awk, grep and git config reads: skill body sizes with frontmatter excluded, CRLF counts, backticked '::' spans across OAW markdown, and the system core.autocrlf value. A grep of graphify/install.py checked how it resolves home directories.
cross_cutting: No absorbed item adds a skill, changes a skill description or edits templates/AGENTS.md (test_skills.py:178-189 caps it at 25 lines; it has 23). Startup-loaded text is unchanged for all 13.

scripts/ are copied into example/minimal-project and example/public-hybrid-demo (sync_examples.py:46-52). Any change to wiki_sync, context_hub or validate_skills, or to templates/docs/raw/_SOURCE_TEMPLATE.md, fails the harness example-content check (harness_check.py:177) until `python scripts/sync_examples.py --write` runs.

harness_check.py:19 MINIMUM_TESTS=159 should rise with each new test, or the new regressions can later disappear unnoticed. harness cli_check (harness_check.py:101-109) only greps --help for subcommand names, so it cannot catch exit-code or message changes.

Seven items target scripts/catalog.py, which does not exist yet (skill-catalog-execution.md:3, :416-419). They cannot regress current OAW. Their tests must ship with catalog.py P2-P4, and a test_catalog module would have to join REQUIRED_TEST_MODULES (harness_check.py:17-18).

Recurring platform hazards: case-insensitive os.path.exists on Windows and macOS, and CRLF from core.autocrlf=true (set at system level on this machine). OAW's own .gitattributes forces eol=lf for *.md, but nothing ships that file to user projects or quarantined foods. Several checks below must normalize line endings or compare exact case to give identical results on the Ubuntu, macOS and Windows CI matrix (README.md:91).
Every absorbed OAW draft still needs its own goldfish review (D10). Behavior-affecting parts, named per item, need improvement.py A/B. Deterministic parts need harness_check tests only.

checks.other_parts_regress: No current test or repo content breaks. OAW markdown outside vendor/ has 0 backticked spans containing '::' (grep), so harness repo-wiki (harness_check.py:178, plain `wiki_sync.py lint`) and installed-lifecycle (:121) stay green, and no test_wiki_sync fixture body contains '::'. The draft must close three regression paths. (1) lint() checks raw bodies (wiki_sync.py:717) and knowledge bodies (:777), and compiled pages embed the raw body verbatim (:314-315), so every bad citation would be reported twice. Check raw notes and manual pages only, and skip build_origin wiki_sync pages. (2) main() catches only ValueError, OSError and RuntimeError (wiki_sync.py:1436). ast.parse raises SyntaxError when a cited file uses newer syntax than the running Python, so lint would crash with a traceback. A decode error or a null byte would abort the whole lint run instead of producing one warning. Contain errors per file and fall back to a regex def/class scan. (3) If bare backticked names count as citations, every `build` or `True` span in user notes becomes an unresolved warning, and --strict turns those into errors (wiki_sync.py:848-849). Only path-qualified forms should count, meaning the left side contains '/' or a file extension. Tests that would catch these, all new in test_wiki_sync: a bad citation is reported once; a cited file with a SyntaxError gives a warning and no 'Traceback' (the pattern of test_missing_refresh_fails_without_traceback, test_wiki_sync.py:268-273); `std::vector` and `crate::x` are not flagged; fenced code is skipped. The _SOURCE_TEMPLATE.md line changes an installer payload file, which trips example-content until the examples are regenerated.
checks.trigger_conflict: None. It adds no skill and changes no description. oaw-wiki already says to run the lint and surface conflicts with current code (templates/.agents/skills/oaw-wiki/SKILL.md:11, :19-21), so the new warnings feed an existing step. The capability overlaps egm-drift-report (docs vs code), but that bridge is disable-model-invocation: true (templates/.agents/skills/egm-drift-report/SKILL.md:5). The upstream entry asks users to add explicit links so drift detection gets cheaper (vendor/egm/skills/egm-drift-report/SKILL.md:28-32), and path::Symbol citations are exactly such links, so the two complement each other.
checks.context_budget: No startup text. The template line is read only when someone writes a raw note. Lint output grows by one line per bad citation. Group warnings per file so a large legacy wiki cannot flood an oaw-wiki turn.
checks.instruction_conflict: Consistent with stdlib-only (re, ast, os), evidence-not-instructions (ast.parse reads code and never executes it) and native-first (no hook, no router). One design constraint follows from existing code: _map_markdown_links deliberately leaves inline code spans alone (wiki_sync.py:489-490), so citations are never rebased. They must be project-root-relative, resolved with confined_path, and an out-of-project path should produce a warning as in _check_links (wiki_sync.py:550-554). The lint itself is deterministic and needs only harness tests. The _SOURCE_TEMPLATE.md convention line is different: it changes what agents write. Per the ledger rule it needs an A/B (the wiki-duel fixture) or must ship after the lint, which stays inert while no note uses the form.
checks.cross_host: One CLI serves both Claude Code and Codex, so no host counterpart is needed. Platform divergence must be designed out. os.path.exists is case-insensitive on Windows and macOS, so `Scripts/Wiki_Sync.py::lint` would pass there and fail on Ubuntu in OAW's own CI matrix; compare exact case with os.listdir. ast grammar depends on the interpreter, and CI runs 3.10 and 3.13, so the regex fallback is also what keeps results identical across versions.
checks.notes: Absorb with four conditions: path-qualified citations only; check raw and manual pages only; contain errors per file with a regex fallback; resolve paths with exact case. Ship the lint before the template line. This draft still needs its own goldfish review (D10).

checks.other_parts_regress: A new read-only subcommand. It inherits every parser condition of gf.code-citation-lint, so lint and cites should share one parser and cannot disagree. Tests that would catch regressions, all new in test_wiki_sync: modify, rename and delete fixtures, where a deleted path still returns the notes citing it; and a byte snapshot of docs/ proving no file changes (the method of test_repeated_build_is_byte_stable_including_meta_pages, test_wiki_sync.py:225-232). Also update the epilog (wiki_sync.py:1291-1306) and the 'Knowledge profile' block of docs/CLI_Reference.md.

The limit is discoverability. oaw-wiki triggers only when wiki maintenance is requested (oaw-wiki/SKILL.md:3), so after a code change an agent finds `cites` only through --help. checks.other_parts_regress: A message-only change in memory_recall. No test asserts the error text: test_recall_* (test_context_hub.py:207-256) check bounds, cursors and a nonzero exit only. The exit status stays 1 (context_hub.py:845-850). Compute the printed minimum with the same candidate() and _render_recall path (context_hub.py:448-457, :476) on the prefix-trimmed, match-only excerpt, so the number is exactly what would succeed. Reading the code (not running it), the :494 error looks unreachable, because the post-loop continuation (:489-491) equals the last fitting candidate's (:454-457). Only :485 needs the number, and :494 can stay as a defensive error. Add a test: at max_chars=512 with a long query, rerunning with the printed number succeeds.
checks.context_budget: Adds one number to an error line and saves agents a retry loop. oaw-evidence calls recall with --max-chars 6000 (oaw-evidence/SKILL.md:14), where the :485 error is rare, so the expected gain is small.
checks.instruction_conflict: None. Stdlib and deterministic. In --json mode the error is still the plain text 'Error: ...' (context_hub.py:849). Keep it that way rather than adding a JSON error schema in the same change.
checks.notes: Small, safe and low value. A deterministic test is enough; no A/B is needed.

checks.other_parts_regress: test_get_and_annotate_reject_traversal_and_missing_topics (test_context_hub.py:65-74) only asserts a nonzero exit, so get on a missing topic returning 4 still passes, and traversal still raises ValueError for exit 1. Correction to the ledger: cli_check (harness_check.py:101-109) only greps --help for subcommand names, so it would NOT catch an exit-code change. New test_context_hub cases are the real guard. Regressions to avoid: (1) `search ''` lists every topic and bootstrap calls search internally (context_hub.py:592, :615), so an empty query or an empty knowledge base must still exit 0. (2) evals/three-way/bench.py:275 counts only commands with exit_code == 0 as successful_commands, so a search with no match would change that recorded metric in later runs. (3) Exit 3 already means 'inconclusive' in improvement.py compare and 'unresolved conflicts' in oaw.py migrate, and exit 2 means malformed input (docs/CLI_Reference.md:16, :73). Using 3 for 'ambiguous' gives it a third meaning, so document the codes per CLI or pick ones that do not collide.
checks.trigger_conflict: None. Skills reach this code through `memory recall` (oaw-evidence/SKILL.md:14), which is unchanged, so default agents see no difference. The side effect is that recall still exits 0 on no match while search would exit 4. Decide that explicitly.
checks.context_budget: Listing candidates adds a few topic ids to stdout. Cap the list, for example at 5.
checks.instruction_conflict: This changes the CLI contract. docs/CLI_Reference.md needs updating, though its current 'Missing topics ... return nonzero' (line 49) stays true, and CHANGELOG and UPGRADING need an entry: a user script running under `set -e` that tolerated a no-match search would now stop. How agents react to a nonzero exit is behavior, since both hosts show it as a failed command, so measure it in an A/B before claiming a benefit.
checks.cross_host: One CLI, and both hosts show exit codes. Today's get already behaves differently per platform: os.path.exists (context_hub.py:243) lets `get topic` find Topic.md on Windows and macOS but not on Linux. Matching candidates case-insensitively forces a choice. Either serve a unique case-insensitive match everywhere (exit 0), or refuse everywhere (exit 3 with candidates), which breaks Windows users who rely on today's lenient match. Choose one and test it on all three CI operating systems.
checks.notes: Absorb only after settling the empty-query rule, the exit-code vocabulary and the case policy, each with new tests. The ledger's claim that cli_check must change is wrong; tests are the guard.

checks.other_parts_regress: Touches only build_origin wiki_sync pages; manual pages are refused at wiki_sync.py:434-438. Builds stay deterministic if the hash is taken over text read by _safe_read (universal newlines, :103-105). In that case test_repeated_build_is_byte_stable_including_meta_pages (test_wiki_sync.py:225-232), test_raw_annotation_heading_does_not_grow_on_refresh (:119-128) and test_legacy_annotations_survive_migration_and_rebuild (:130-143) keep passing. Three regression paths: (1) Pages compiled before this change have no hash field. Lint must treat absence as 'unknown', or every existing user wiki fails lint after migrate. (2) If a renderer-version mismatch is reported as an issue, every project's `wiki_sync lint`, including CI that runs it, fails after each OAW upgrade until a rebuild. Report it as a warning, and as an error only under --strict. (3) Hashing raw bytes would mark pages built on POSIX as stale on Windows: this machine has core.autocrlf=true at system level, and OAW's eol=lf .gitattributes is not shipped to user projects. Add a golden test that fails when _render_topic_page output changes without a RENDERER_VERSION bump.
checks.context_budget: Nothing loads at startup, but `context_hub get` prints compiled-page frontmatter in full (context_hub.py:247-248) and recall scans it (:431-436). A full 64-hex sha256 costs about 40 tokens per source, so a page with 10 sources adds roughly 400-500 tokens to every get. Use short digests per source (12-16 hex); this is a staleness signal, not a security boundary.
checks.instruction_conflict: Consistent with Wiki_Sync_Guide.md:18, which makes stale source/page comparisons lint errors, and :16, which promises stable output for unchanged inputs. Stdlib hashlib. The frontmatter must stay inside _parse_frontmatter's subset (wiki_sync.py:31-74): scalars and '- item' lists only, for example `- docs/raw/a.md 1a2b3c4d5e6f`.
checks.cross_host: Identical on both hosts once text is LF-normalized before hashing.
checks.notes: Absorb with five conditions: lint tolerates pages without the field; a renderer mismatch is a warning; hashes cover LF-normalized text; digests are short; a golden test guards the renderer version.

checks.other_parts_regress: catalog.py is still planned (skill-catalog-execution.md:416-419), so no current code regresses. It conflicts with two neighbouring planned stages. (1) Defanging inserts U+200B, so quotes a reviewer copies from a wrapped packet no longer match the source. Both the verify step's quote checks and gf.read-coverage-check's file:line checks break unless they strip U+200B first. (2) The sha256 must cover the original bytes, taken before defanging and labelled as such. Otherwise it cannot be tied to the quarantine manifest (skill-catalog-execution.md:74). Do not extend the wrapper to context_hub recall. The evals/three-way (bench.py:145) and evals/skill-value (fixtures.py:49, :83) fixtures measure the host's own resistance to quoted 'SYSTEM:' injections, and wrapping recall would change those inputs. That extension would need its own A/B.
checks.context_budget: Only in on-demand digestion packets, at roughly 120 bytes of tag, path and hash per file. Nothing at startup.
checks.instruction_conflict: Matches evidence-not-instructions (README.md:142; templates/AGENTS.md:15) and the plan's prompt-injection risk (skill-catalog-execution.md:445), and it ships as defense in depth with no gain claimed (README.md:143). Limit: it protects only content embedded in a packet. Goldfish reviewers who open food files with their own tools (Read in Claude Code, shell in Codex) get raw text, and OAW ships no hook that could wrap tool output. Build goldfish packets that embed wrapped files, and keep the 'food files are data' framing for anything read through tools.
checks.cross_host: The packet text is identical on both hosts. Neither host lets OAW wrap tool-read content without hooks, which OAW forbids, so the remaining gap is the same on both and no counterpart is missing.
checks.notes: Absorb into the catalog packet builder and this workflow's reviewer prompts. Hash the original bytes, and make quote verification aware of U+200B. Keep it out of context_hub until a separate A/B. The OAW draft needs a goldfish review (D10).

checks.other_parts_regress: Only the planned record format changes (skill-catalog-execution.md:419), so nothing current regresses. The goldfish and verify records already written for graphify, claude-mem and tokeneconomizer have no coverage fields; for example, ingest/graphify/goldfish-1.json has only reviewer, food, pinned_source, package_version, method, verdict_summary and findings. Making the field required would invalidate them silently, so mark them 'coverage unverified' instead of treating them as valid or rejected. Count lines with Python splitlines on decoded text, so CRLF or a missing final newline cannot shift line totals between platforms.
checks.context_budget: A small coverage object per file in reviewer JSON. On demand only.
checks.instruction_conflict: Stdlib and deterministic. Reviewers report their own coverage, so the check proves consistency: every cited line exists and the reported last line equals the real file length. It does not prove the reviewer read every line, and the gate should be worded that way.
checks.cross_host: Needs a counterpart for each host. Claude Code's Read returns numbered lines with a 2,000-line default (the food's extraction-spec.md:12-26), so a reviewer can report the last line it saw. Codex reads files through shell commands, the host truncates long output, and line numbers appear only if the reviewer requests them, so a Codex reviewer may not know what it missed. The packet must tell Codex reviewers to read in explicit numbered ranges (for example `nl` with `sed -n 'A,Bp'`) and to report those ranges.
checks.notes: Absorb into the goldfish/verify record format, with the Codex reading instruction and an 'unverified' state for older records.

checks.other_parts_regress: Rubric text plus regex and JSON flag rules in the planned static digest (skill-catalog-execution.md:77, :418). No runtime code is added and nothing existing changes.
checks.context_budget: About 2 KB, loaded into a digest packet only when a food ships hooks. Nothing at startup.
checks.instruction_conflict: The items must stay flag-only and never auto-reject, because the plan requires human judgement after EGM's 'bypass' hits all turned out benign (skill-catalog-execution.md:77, :274). One wording fix: the ledger says 'the same list applies to any future OAW hook', which can read as licence to add hooks. OAW ships none, and its packaging allowlist rejects them (skill-catalog-execution.md:313), so limit the rubric to judging foods. The '600 s host default' timeout comes from the food's own comment (graphify/install.py:477-511). Check it against current host docs before encoding it as a number.
checks.cross_host: Host-neutral if each item names both config surfaces, .claude/settings.json hooks and .codex/hooks.json. Items based on Claude hook payload fields, such as session_id and agent_id for the nudge budget, must not be required of Codex hooks, whose payloads differ. Judge Codex hooks on timeout, fail-open behavior and scope.
checks.notes: Absorb as flag-only rubric items for foods, with the wording fix.

checks.other_parts_regress: No OAW code is touched. The risk is to the user's machine, not to OAW tests.
checks.instruction_conflict: As written, this conflicts with current policy. Running a food's installer executes untrusted code. D7 says quarantined repos are 'never executed during digestion', and the plan forbids running third-party install scripts during ingestion (skill-catalog-execution.md:431). D11 allows trial runs only inside a standing sandbox policy that the owner sets once, and DECISIONS.md records no such policy yet. graphify's installer also needs its package installed first, and pip or uv then runs a build backend, so the check executes more than the installer. It must stay off until that policy exists.
checks.cross_host: A 'throwaway HOME' does not isolate anything on Windows. The food resolves its targets through Path.home() (graphify/install.py:62, :214-260, :999, :2302) and LOCALAPPDATA (:224-226), and Python 3.8+ on Windows ignores HOME and uses USERPROFILE. A Windows run would therefore write into the real profile, which is an unconsented edit of host settings. Any run needs USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE/HOMEPATH, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL redirected, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, the network off, and a before/after snapshot of the real profile, or better a disposable VM or container. It must exercise both the claude and the codex install paths.
checks.notes: Do not force it in; move it to hold. Blockers: the D11 sandbox policy and a Windows-safe isolation spec. Three parts can be absorbed now at no cost. (1) The no-execution replica pattern (scratchpad/ledger-work/h1_replica.py) as a fixture test. (2) A static inventory of the installer's write targets. (3) A pass criterion of 'every touched file restored byte-for-byte, new files listed', since rolling backups such as .graphify-bak are legitimate leftovers.

checks.other_parts_regress: Targets the planned ingest record (skill-catalog-execution.md:74, :417), so nothing existing regresses. wiki_sync and context_hub are correctly left alone, because they read only *.md (wiki_sync.py:146-150).
checks.context_budget: Makes packets smaller. Nothing at startup.
checks.instruction_conflict: Aligned with AGENTS.md:20, which keeps credentials out of the public repository. It conflicts with the plan's ingest gate, though. That gate records the file list and hashes (skill-catalog-execution.md:74), and catalog evidence is meant to live in the repository (:258). A published sha256 of a short, low-entropy secret (.netrc, .pgpass) allows offline dictionary confirmation, so record only path and size for flagged files. The patterns also over-match. .env.example, .env.sample and .env.template usually hold no secrets but show which keys a food reads, which is central to findings like gf.llm-backend-autodetect. Allow them with values redacted instead of excluding them.
checks.cross_host: The filter runs in catalog.py, so it behaves the same on both hosts; enforcement during tool reads differs. For Claude reviewer sessions OAW already builds permissions.deny settings (evals/egm-pilot/run_pilot.py:110-116), so a Read deny on flagged paths is mechanical. OAW has no verified per-path read deny for Codex reviewers (evals/three-way/bench.py:262 uses codex exec flags only), so on Codex the rule stays prose. Record that asymmetry.
checks.notes: Absorb with no hashes for flagged files, redacted .env templates and a recorded Codex enforcement asymmetry.

checks.other_parts_regress: Targets only the planned ingest code (skill-catalog-execution.md:229, :417), so nothing existing regresses.
checks.instruction_conflict: Consistent with using the network only when asked (skill-catalog-execution.md:432) and reading tokens only from the environment (:108). URL checks alone miss git's own escape routes, so the draft must also constrain git itself. Allow only https (`-c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always`), which blocks ext::, fd:: and file://. Do not recurse into submodules, whose URLs would bypass validation. Set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Turn off LFS smudge (GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1), because a repo's .lfsconfig can point lfs.url at any host, an SSRF path the host allowlist never sees. https-only also rejects SSH remotes, so document that private repos go through the plan's local-directory path.
checks.cross_host: Windows differs. Git for Windows' credential manager can open a GUI prompt on a 401 (a private or misspelled repo) and hang a headless ingest even with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Pass `-c credential.helper=` (and GCM_INTERACTIVE=never) during ingest. Otherwise one CLI behaves the same under Claude Code and Codex.
checks.notes: Absorb with git transport, LFS and credential controls added. For a git-only fetch these matter more than the IP-range checks.

checks.other_parts_regress: Only the planned evidence format changes, so nothing existing regresses. As the ledger says, improvement.py keeps its raw-byte digests (improvement.py:29-30, :46-53).
checks.instruction_conflict: Hash-basis conflict. OAW already uses two bases: raw bytes in improvement.py, and CRLF folded to LF in evals/egm-pilot/pilot_common.py:41, recorded as 'hash_basis' in convert_scenarios.py:377. graphify's fingerprint also strips trailing whitespace, which would add a third. Reuse pilot_common's CRLF-fold basis and record hash_basis. For EGM persona rubrics, cite the per-file upstream sha256 that vendor/egm/OAW_SOURCE.json already holds (for example :45) instead of hashing again. Fingerprint only the fixed rubric, not the per-food packet, or every review will hash differently. Existing goldfish records carry no fingerprint, so mark them 'rubric unknown' rather than valid.
checks.cross_host: Host-specific preambles, such as Agent versus spawn_agent dispatch, would give different prompt hashes. Record the host in a separate field and hash only the shared rubric, so Claude and Codex evidence for the same rubric match.
checks.notes: Absorb using OAW's existing CRLF-fold basis, a rubric-only scope and a host field.

checks.other_parts_regress: Every current package passes any body gate: measured template bodies, frontmatter excluded, are 797 to 1,354 bytes, so test_only_scoped_native_packages_are_shipped (test_skills.py:168-176) stays green. lint_skill_file also runs inside `wiki_sync lint` (wiki_sync.py:838-840) and doctor, so a gate added there also applies to project-owned custom versions of OAW packages, which are in the managed+custom scope (validate_skills.py:133-145). The message should say so. The bundled EGM upstream bodies sit close to the limit: egm-bootstrap is 23,610 bytes, 390 under (matching skill-catalog-execution.md:272), and egm-review is 22,129. Those files are hash-locked (vendor/egm/OAW_SOURCE.json:45, checked by sync_egm.py --check-bundled at harness_check.py:174), so they can never be split into references/. For pinned vendored runtimes the remedy must say 'hold this upstream version or record an exception', not 'move text to references/'.
checks.trigger_conflict: None. No description changes, and the EGM bridges stay disable-model-invocation: true.
checks.context_budget: Positive, since references load on demand and keep invocation bodies small. The measured quantity needs a definition, though. A bridge tells the agent to read the complete upstream entry (templates/.agents/skills/egm-bootstrap/SKILL.md:10-12), so the real load at invocation is about 1,348 + 23,610 bytes, over 24,000, while the bridge alone is 1.3 KB. Measuring only the bridge lets the bridge pattern sidestep the gate. The startup budget is unaffected, because the plan measures only name and description at startup (skill-catalog-execution.md:120).
checks.instruction_conflict: Consistent with proof-before-promotion and with the gate the plan adopted from EGM (skill-catalog-execution.md:76, :215, :311). graphify shows the remedy's limit: after moving about 49 KB into references/, its bodies are still about 48 KB.
checks.cross_host: Platform divergence: the gate must count LF-normalized UTF-8 bytes. With CRLF, egm-bootstrap's 421-line body grows to 24,031 bytes, so a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true (this machine's system setting) would fail while POSIX passes. OAW's own .gitattributes forces eol=lf for *.md and sets vendor/egm/** to -text, but quarantined foods and user projects get no such file. Claude Code and Codex both load SKILL.md at invocation and references on demand, so host behavior is otherwise identical.
checks.notes: Absorb the remedy message with three additions: an LF-normalized byte count, an exception path for hash-locked vendored runtimes, and an explicit rule for measuring a bridge plus its upstream entry.
